requirements_summary.summary: Participium is a web application for the Municipality of Turin enabling citizens to report urban issues (e.g., potholes, trash) via an interactive map or Telegram bot. Reports undergo a lifecycle from submission and approval by a Public Relations Officer to assignment, execution (by internal staff or external maintainers), and resolution. The system supports role-based access for citizens, municipal staff, administrators, and external partners, with features for notifications, statistics, and two-way communication.

requirements.text:
As an unregistered user
I want to see approved reports on an interactive map 
So that I can know about issues in my area and beyond.
expected_behaviors: I can know about issues in my area and beyond

requirements.text:
As a technical office staff member
I want to assign reports to external maintainers
So that specialized maintainers can handle and update the intervention.
constraints: It can be possible for specific reports of certain categories (e.g., Enel X for category Public Lighting) based on their content reviewed by the technical office staff member.
expected_behaviors: specialized maintainers can handle and update the intervention

requirements.text:
As an external maintainer 
I want to update the status of a report assigned to me
So that I can updated citizens about  the intervention.
expected_behaviors: I can updated citizens about  the intervention

requirements.text:
As a technical office staff member/external maintainer
I want to exchange information and comments on the report internally
So that coordination happens without exposing internal notes to citizens
expected_behaviors: coordination happens without exposing internal notes to citizens

requirements.text:
As a citizen
I want to register with my name and username 
So that I can access the Participium system and submit reports.
constraints: Registration is required before submitting reports.
expected_behaviors: I can access the Participium system and submit reports

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to confirm my registration with a code
So that my account becomes valid and I can start using the system.
constraints: Once a registration is completed, the user gets an email with a confirmation code. The person can use the application only after confirming by entering the code valid for 30 minutes.
expected_behaviors: my account becomes valid and I can start using the system

requirements.text:
As a system administrator
I want to set up municipality users
constraints: These are the internal accounts of the municipality

requirements.text:
As a system administrator
I want to assign roles to municipality users
constraints: Possible roles: municipal public relations officer, municipal administrator, technical office staff member, external maintainer. You can be more specific on technical offices to run realisti scenarios following the official organizational structure of the municipality of Turin (https://trasparenza.comune.torino.it/media/2212/download)

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to provide details for my report 
So that the the problem is classified correctly.
constraints: Mandatory fields: title, description,  category , photos (min 1 max 3).
expected_behaviors: the the problem is classified correctly

requirements.text:
As a municipal public relations officer
I want to review and approve or reject reports 
So that only valid reports are processed further.
constraints: Rejected reports must include an explanation. If accepted, the report is assigned to the technical office bound to the report category.
expected_behaviors: only valid reports are processed further

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to see approved reports on an interactive map 
So that I can know about issues in my area and beyond.
constraints: Map should be zoomable. When zooming out, reports can be grouped into a cumulative report for a better visualization (total number should be reported on the cumulative report). When zooming in,  reports can be seen separated, with their title and reporter name (or "anonymous" if this is flagged on that report).
expected_behaviors: I can know about issues in my area and beyond

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to choose whether to make my report anonymous 
So that my name is not shown in the public list of reports.
constraints: Anonymous option protects privacy. Choice made at issue description time.
expected_behaviors: my name is not shown in the public list of reports

requirements.text:
As a technical office staff member
I want to see the list of reports assigned to me
So that I can get an overview of the maintenance to be done
expected_behaviors: I can get an overview of the maintenance to be done

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to configure my account
So that I can better manage notifications and my virtual presence.
constraints: Citizens can  upload a personal photo, add their Telegram username and switch off/on email notifications in the configuration panel.
expected_behaviors: I can better manage notifications and my virtual presence

requirements.text:
As a system administrator
I want to modify roles to municipality users
So that the staff can be more flexible.
constraints: This story overwrites a previous answer given by PO on the Telegram chat. NB: 1) A municipality user can now have multiple roles, i.e. serving on more than one technical office. 2) Modification includes cancellation.
expected_behaviors: the staff can be more flexible

requirements.text:
As a technical office staff member 
I want to update report statuses 
So that citizens are informed of the problem resolution process.
constraints: At each status change, the citizen receives notification in the platform with the corresponding update. Municipal operators working on reports can also send messages to the citizens in the platform, to which the citizen can reply.
expected_behaviors: citizens are informed of the problem resolution process

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to reply to messages from municipal operators in the platform 
So that I can communicate directly about my report.
constraints: Two-way communication is possible within the platform.
expected_behaviors: I can communicate directly about my report

requirements.text:
As a citizen 
I want to receive optional email alerts in addition to platform notifications 
So that I can choose the best way to stay updated.
constraints: Unless disabled in their configuration panel.
expected_behaviors: I can choose the best way to stay updated

requirements.text:
As a citizen/unregistered user
I want to browse a summary table of reports with filters 
So that I can easily explore and analyze existing reports.
constraints: Filters: by category, status, period of time
expected_behaviors: I can easily explore and analyze existing reports

domain_rules: Reports must be in 'Pending Approval' state until the Organization Office performs preliminary verification.
Accepted reports move to 'Assigned'; Rejected reports require an explanation; Resolved reports close the issue.
Possible statuses: Pending Approval, Assigned, In Progress, Suspended, Rejected, Resolved.
External maintainers can only update status if they have access to Participium (Case 1).
Internal comments between technical office and external maintainer are reserved and not visible to the reporter.
Only authenticated users (citizens) can view reports initially; unregistered users can also view reports from Sprint 4 onwards.
An anonymous user's name is visible to staff but hidden in the public Turin map for citizens.
Once a report is inserted, it cannot be modified or deleted by the citizen.
Public Relation Officer can assign a report either to a specific technical office or directly to a staff member.
Only technical office staff members can have multiple roles.
Email is mandatory for registration and can be used for login.
Confirmation code for registration is valid for 30 minutes.
Mandatory fields for reports: title, description, category, photos (min 1 max 3).
Categories include: Water Supply, Architectural Barriers, Sewer System, Public Lighting, Waste, Road Signs and Traffic Lights, Roads and Urban Furnishings, Public Green Areas and Playgrounds, Other.
Map layer must be based on OpenStreetMap (standard layer).
Automatic assignment of issues is possible only if previously set by the municipal administrator.
edge_cases: External maintainer resolves a report without moving it to 'In Progress' first (if allowed by workflow), or moves directly from 'Assigned' to 'Resolved'.
Citizen follows a report that is later resolved; system must stop sending notifications once status becomes 'Resolved'.
User attempts to download CSV with no filters applied vs. with filters applied; system must handle both data subsets correctly.
Telegram bot receives a command for a non-existent report ID; system must handle gracefully (e.g., error message).
Registration code expires before confirmation; user cannot activate account until re-registration or new code generation.
assumptions: The 'Organization Office' refers to the central administrative body responsible for initial review.
Competent technical office is determined by the problem category (e.g., Public Lighting -> Enel X or specific office).
Telegram bot integration requires a valid Telegram API connection and user authentication via username.
Push notifications are sent via Telegram API; email notifications use SMTP.
The 'top 1% of reporters' statistic is calculated based on the total number of reports submitted by each reporter.
Unregistered users viewing reports do not have access to submission or editing features.

authentication_notes: /sessions POST is the only unauthenticated endpoint; all other endpoints require valid session from createSession or are public read-only (listApprovedReports, createUploadUrl).
/citizens/verify-email depends on prior creation of verification code via /citizens/verification-code.
/admin/* and /reports/* operations require elevated roles (admin, technical officer, maintainer) as implied by 403 responses.
Operations marked auth_required need an authenticated session during test setup.
dependencies: /sessions POST is prerequisite for all auth-required endpoints. /registration POST allows new citizen accounts without prior login. /citizens/verification-code must precede /citizens/verify-email. Admin operations (/admin/*) depend on user creation via /admin/createuser. Report operations (/reports/*) depend on report creation via /reports POST.
Chat and notification endpoints depend on existing reports or sessions.
POST /reports -> GET /chats/{reportId}: A report must exist before an operation can address reportId.
POST /reports -> POST /chats/{reportId}/read: A report must exist before an operation can address reportId.
POST /sessions -> GET /sessions/current: getCurrentSession requires an active session created by createSession.
POST /citizens/verification-code -> POST /citizens/verify-email: verifyCitizenEmail requires an active verification code generated by createCitizenVerificationCode.
POST /admin/createuser -> POST /admin/addcategory: addOperatorCategory requires an existing operator created by createMunicipalityUser.
POST /reports -> PUT /reports/{id}/status: updateReportStatus requires an existing report created by createReport.
POST /reports -> PUT /reports/{id}/operator: assignReportOperator requires an existing report created by createReport.

risks: /citizens/verify-email may fail if verification code expires (423) without explicit expiry handling in client. /admin/* endpoints lack explicit role checks in documentation; 403 responses imply hidden role requirements. Route name 'mainteiner' is non-standard and may cause confusion or typos in client implementations.
listApprovedReports is public but depends on report creation flow; no clear mechanism to filter by category or status beyond 'approved'.
Notification and chat endpoints rely on session state that may be invalidated by deleteCurrentSession without explicit cleanup guidance.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Unregistered user can view approved reports on an interactive map.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute a GET request to /reports/approved without any authentication headers. Verify that the response returns a list of report objects containing only public fields (e.g., title, status, location) and excludes sensitive internal comments or user emails.
strategy_items.rationale: Validates the core requirement that unregistered users can access public data without authentication.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Unregistered user can view approved reports on an interactive map.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute a GET request to /reports/approved without authentication. Verify that the response returns a list of report objects containing only public fields (e.g., title, status, location) and excludes sensitive internal comments or user emails.
strategy_items.rationale: Tests the edge case where an unregistered user accesses the API without any prior setup, ensuring data privacy constraints are met.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Technical office staff member assigns reports to external maintainers.
strategy_items.prompt: Authenticate as a 'technical_office_staff_member'. Execute a PUT request to /reports/{id}/mainteiner with an invalid maintainer ID (non-existent user). Verify that the system returns an appropriate error code (e.g., 404 or 400) and does not create an assignment.
setup_needed: Create a report via POST /reports with mandatory fields.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Verify no resource was created; delete the report using DELETE /reports/{id} if it still exists.
strategy_items.rationale: Tests negative behavior where an invalid maintainer ID is provided, ensuring the system handles errors gracefully.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Technical office staff member updates report statuses.
strategy_items.prompt: Authenticate as a 'technical_office_staff_member'. Execute a PUT request to /reports/{id}/status with status 'Suspended' and then immediately attempt to update it again to 'Resolved' without proper workflow steps. Verify that the system enforces the correct state transitions.
setup_needed: Assign the report to a technical office or staff member via PUT /reports/{id}/mainteiner.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Delete the created report using DELETE /reports/{id} after verification.
strategy_items.rationale: Tests stateful workflow where multiple status updates are performed in sequence, ensuring correct state management.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Citizen registers with name and username to access the system.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute a happy path registration. Provide a valid JSON body with 'name', 'username', and 'email'. Expect a success response indicating account creation pending verification.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Delete created resources or restore their previous state.
strategy_items.rationale: Validates the core entry point for new users as per PT01.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Citizen confirms registration with a code to activate account.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute the happy path for email verification. First, call /citizens/verification-code (auth_required: true) to generate a valid code. Then, call /citizens/verify-email with that code in the body. Expect account activation.
setup_needed: Call POST /citizens/verification-code to obtain a valid verification code.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Delete created resources or restore their previous state.
strategy_items.rationale: Validates the stateful workflow required by PT27 and domain rules regarding confirmation codes.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Technical office staff exchanges internal comments on a report.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute the happy path for adding an internal comment. Use an authenticated session with role 'technical_office_staff'. Provide a JSON body with 'content' and optionally 'author_id'. Expect success.
setup_needed: Ensure an existing report ID is available (e.g., create a dummy report or use a known ID).
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Delete created resources or restore their previous state.
strategy_items.rationale: Validates the internal communication channel defined in PT26.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: Citizen replies to messages from municipal operators in the platform.
strategy_items.prompt: Execute a stateful workflow for messaging. First, ensure an authenticated citizen session exists. Then, POST a message to /reports/{id}/messages with 'sender_id' (operator) and 'content'. Verify the message is created.
setup_needed: Ensure an existing report ID is available.
Ensure an authenticated citizen session exists.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Delete created resources or restore their previous state.
strategy_items.rationale: Validates the chat functionality defined in PT18 and API analysis for message creation.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: System administrator assigns roles to municipality users.
strategy_items.prompt: Create a new municipality user with a specific role assigned (e.g., 'technical_office_staff') using the admin session. Ensure the payload includes valid email and password fields required for registration.
setup_needed: Authenticate as system administrator to obtain a valid session token.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Delete created resources or restore their previous state.
strategy_items.rationale: Validates the core functionality of creating users with roles, which is a prerequisite for other admin operations like assigning categories or modifying roles.

strategy_items.requirement_summary: System administrator modifies roles to municipality users.
strategy_items.prompt: Update an existing municipality user's role from 'citizen' to 'technical_office_staff' using the admin session. Include all necessary fields for a successful update.
setup_needed: Create a test user via POST /admin/createuser to have an ID to modify.
strategy_items.cleanup_strategy: Delete the created test user via DELETE /citizens/{id} if it was not intended to persist, or verify no resource was created if the update failed unexpectedly.
strategy_items.rationale: Tests the ability of administrators to flexibly modify user roles as per requirement PT10.
